item.title: SpaceX is about to attempt the ‘holy grail’ of rocketry
item.description: “It’s hard to overstate the significance” of the Starship launch scheduled to take place on Friday, analyst says Fuente: MarketWatch.
item.dc:creator: William Gavin

item.title: Ancient height trends show technological advances did not always improve living standards
item.description: New research from the University of Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in Jena gives valuable clues as to economic development in various regions across thousands of years. Researchers evaluated 18,457 skeletal remains and analyzed changes in height, estimated from thighbone length. The bones come from 45 different countries across Europe and Asia. The study has been published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Written in sand: How dunes reveal the secrets of planetary winds
item.description: Stanford University researchers have shown that the median sand grain size in dunes on Earth and Mars reveals the speed of the winds that formed those dunes. The finding enables scientists to use sand as a wind speedometer for both modern and ancient dunes found across the solar system. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How woodcocks evolved to be the weird cousins of their family
item.description: A woodcock is an odd little bird with a long, skinny bill and a plump, chunky body that's shaped like an American football. It mostly hangs out near the ground, but it does a mating display in which it makes a buzzy, tweeting call and then takes off zigzagging across the sky. The woodcock stands out from most of the members of its family, the sandpipers. The majority of sandpiper species are champion migrators that traverse thousands of miles every year, but many woodcock species and their closest cousins, the snipes, have evolved to migrate shorter distances. Some island-dwelling species of… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Songs from same genre or era evoke similar memories across listeners
item.description: The first few notes of an electric guitar can send memories from your teenage years rushing back. These memories often feel intensely personal. But a new study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences finds that the memories evoked by songs are surprisingly similar from person to person and vary with a song's genre and decade. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Navigating lunar orbit using nothing but shadows and a power meter
item.description: Humanity is quickly reaching the limits of our ability to track all the satellites we have in deep space. NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) has been the workhorse for tracking them for decades but is quickly being overwhelmed by the number of requests it receives, which in turn makes it harder to track some recently launched missions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study reveals immune cells' ability to engulf and destroy amoebae
item.description: More than 100 million severe infections are believed to be caused worldwide each year by various species of amoebae, single-celled organisms typically found in freshwater and saltwater and moist environments. While treatment with antibiotics for these infections is often effective, scientists have long believed the body's own immune cells were unable to defend against amoebae. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI and experiments reveal impurities hindering waste plastic pyrolysis oil recycling
item.description: A Korean research team has identified how impurities interfere with the use of waste plastic pyrolysis oil as a petrochemical feedstock through catalytic experiments and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational chemistry. The findings, published in the journal ACS Catalysis, provide a scientific basis for predicting potential declines in catalytic performance according to the types and concentrations of impurities present. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Video shows rocket failure that destroys 40 Amazon satellites
item.description: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket suffered an in-flight failure minutes after liftoff from Florida, leaving 40 Amazon internet satellites unable to reach orbit. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: 'Forced fighters' are being lured into Ukraine war under false pretenses
item.description: Ukraine recently captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war. According to the Ukrainian state-run I Want to Live project, the 49-year-old man from Java had been promised work in Russia's construction industry only to realize he had been recruited into the army while being transported to Donetsk. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Elusive optical effect paves the way for advanced lidar and nanophotonic technologies
item.description: An international research team, led by scientists from Skoltech, has experimentally demonstrated for the first time the photonic spin Hall shift for light scattered off an optically small particle. This work, published in the Advanced Photonics journal, overcomes a long-standing challenge in optics and could contribute to the development of next-generation optical technologies, advanced radar and lidar systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study of juries' decision-making addresses disagreement among jurors
item.description: A new study shows that understanding decisions made by juries requires attention not only to their final verdicts but also to how jurors make decisions individually and work together to reach a verdict, especially when they disagree. Led by Tova Cohen, a Ph.D. student at Rutgers School of Criminal Justice, the research studied 35 participants in seven virtual mock juries to examine individuals' characteristics, deliberative participation, changed verdicts and dissent. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mogging is the word of the year—but men have been doing it since Shakespearean times
item.description: The Collins English Dictionary has selected "mogging" as its 2026 word of the year. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sentinel-6B in Orbit Around Earth
item.description: Description This artist’s concept shows the Sentinel-6B satellite, which will become the reference satellite for other missions studying sea surface height. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: One wandering plume may have created several Atlantic volcanic chains
item.description: Beneath the North Atlantic Ocean lies a series of underwater volcanic mountain chains stretching from the coast of North America toward the Azores. These include the New England Seamounts and the Great Meteor Seamounts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rare North Atlantic right whale population drops, alarming scientists
item.description: The population of one of the world's rarest whales has fallen after trending upward in recent years, worrying scientists who fear the animal could still be at risk of extinction. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Protecting forests outside parks benefits the birds within
item.description: Every year, around 3.5 billion birds migrate to North America to breed, finding safe havens and nesting grounds in our national parks along the way. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: City crows and country crows don't see the world the same way
item.description: A country crow hesitates upon seeing a takeout food box. A city crow pauses the first time it sees an ear of corn. Both are taken aback when they find a strange wooden object next to the expected peanuts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Thunderbirds in Formation
item.description: U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds fighter jets pass overhead during the agency’s MAX POWER expo and air show on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA’s inaugural MAX POWER was an aerospace festival celebrating the past, present, and future of flight and space exploration in honor of America’s 250th anniversary. Image […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: From 400 miles above Earth, AI tracks invasive leafy spurge
item.description: Harnessing satellite imagery, AI deep-learning models and community science data, scientists from the University of Minnesota have tracked the spread of leafy spurge over a 20-year period. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient tree rings and ice cores help pin down when Babylonia fell
item.description: We know quite a lot about ancient Mesopotamia, the historical region spanning modern-day Iraq and parts of Syria and Turkey, such as who ruled and the order in which kings succeeded one another. But pinning down exact calendar dates for historical events has been trickier. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New ethical approach to environmental issues would avoid 'problem shifting,' law scholar says
item.description: When governments have attempted to address environmental problems in recent decades, they have often simply shifted the problem elsewhere or created a new problem for others. A University of Kansas law professor is among a group of scholars who published a study pointing out such environmental problem shifting and proposing "strange loop ethics" as a method to rethink critical legal issues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why forest fires often break out simultaneously across Europe
item.description: Firefighting aircraft, helicopters, fire departments—when forests across Europe are burning at the same time, the limited firefighting resources have to be allocated efficiently, and ideally before the fires even break out. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christina Koch, astronauta de Artemis II: qué dijo sobre la repercusión de la misión en la Tierra
item.description: Tras su regreso a la Tierra, Donald Trump le entregó a cada tripulante una medalla Medalla de Honor Espacial del Congreso, durante una ceremonia en el Centro Espacial Jonhson de Houston Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Giving an insider's perspective could help rural destinations attract more support from tourists
item.description: From helping fellow tourists find their way to recommending independent shops and local businesses, visitors can play a part in supporting rural communities. New research suggests that the way destinations communicate their social values could encourage more support. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Deadly virus reduces tree frog population by 83% in Atlantic Forest reserve
item.description: A highly lethal pathogen is responsible for the mass death of tadpoles and the rapid decline of amphibian populations in the Atlantic Forest. A group of researchers demonstrate for the first time in South America that recurring ranavirus outbreaks caused an 83% drop in monkey frog (Phyllomedusa distincta) reproduction in a pond in the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. The disease is caused by a virus that affects reptiles and fish as well. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Q&A: How can consumers reduce food waste around the holidays?
item.description: Fans of Thanksgiving look forward each year to family traditions and a table full of holiday dishes. Less anticipated is the aftermath: cleaning up and deciding what to do with all those leftovers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dirty ice around young star Beta Pictoris suggests frequent collisions and sheds light on the system's formation
item.description: In a recent study of infrared light collected by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a group of astronomers detected ice for the first time around the young star Beta Pictoris. Researchers had expected ice around Beta Pictoris, but previous searches had not directly detected it. The study, published in Science, found that the ice is mostly noncrystalline and mixed with carbon dioxide. The team says these new details provide clues about the early formation of the Beta Pictoris system and collisions that may still be occurring. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Team maximizes efficiency of heavy rare-earth elements for high-performance permanent magnets
item.description: Neodymium–iron–boron (Nd–Fe–B) permanent magnets are key components in electric vehicle traction motors and wind turbines. In particular, heavy rare-earth elements, which are added to maintain coercivity (resistance to demagnetization) even at high temperatures, are extremely expensive and have unstable supply chains, consequently placing a significant burden on industry. Since completely eliminating heavy rare-earth elements remains difficult, the most important technical challenge is to minimize their use while maintaining magnetic performance. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Satellite radar tracks lava flows and crater changes at Hawaii's Kilauea volcano
item.description: The slow-moving lava of an effusive volcanic eruption can transform a landscape. But escaping gases, cloud cover, accessibility issues and limited local resources can make monitoring the development of a flow field dangerous and difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Groundwater's annual cycle is shifting: 50-year study in Finland reveals contrasting outcomes in the north and south
item.description: The annual cycle of Finland's groundwater has changed over the past 50 years, shows a long-term study by the University of Oulu and the Finnish Environment Institute. The findings provide a valuable reference point for examining groundwater change in other northern regions: shallow, fast-responding aquifers occur worldwide. The paper is published in the Journal of Hydrology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Model of 'alpha-beta decay' could solve a decades-old nuclear mystery
item.description: A pair of researchers has created a new model for radioactive decay, which allows alpha and beta decay to happen simultaneously in a single transition. Testing their model's predictions against a full chart of known isotopes, Wenqiang Zhang at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, together with Chong Qi at the Alba Nova University Centre, Stockholm, showed that these simultaneous emissions could better explain the observed emission spectra of several radioactive isotopes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reading superconducting qubits while suppressing unwanted state transitions
item.description: Recently an artificial intelligence proved an 18-year-old conjecture in computer science, called the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture. The proof settles a long-standing conjecture (educated guess) that eliminates one proposed route to enormous quantum computer speedups, ruling out one particular variant of "quantum supremacy," the term for the hypothesis that a programmable quantum computer can solve a problem that no classical computer can solve in any "feasible" amount of time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jim Mirandy
item.description: The rumble of a rocket engine might be considered a soundtrack for Jim Mirandy’s life. Mirandy has grown up with NASA as a constant presence, and his path to becoming a civil servant at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, has been decades in the making. Hired under the agency’s workforce directive […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: LaToya Dean

item.title: Amazon pierde 40 satélites tras la explosión de un cohete Vulcan: es un gran revés a sus ambiciosos planes
item.description: Por si el pique entre Elon Musk y Jeff Bezos no fuese ya algo legendario, este fin de semana el azar-o la tecnología- ha llevado sus diferencias a otro nivel. El CEO de SpaceX ha hecho historia recuperando por primera vez en el aire la segunda etapa de uno de sus Starship. Este, además, venía de depositar 26 satélites de nueva generación en su constelación Starlink. 24 horas después de este hito, Amazon pretendía añadir también unos cuantos satélites más a su propia constelación, pero en su caso, en vez de un éxito, todo terminó en desastre, con un fallo del cohete que los transportaba que… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder
item.description: Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that this common vitamin could inspire new treatments for rare genetic diseases. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought
item.description: Scientists have discovered that the heart ages unevenly, with surprising hotspots of inflammation and scarring concentrated in the valves and major blood vessels rather than the heart muscle. The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about cardiac aging and could help researchers develop new ways to protect the heart as we grow older. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
item.description: NASA is offering $1 million in its new Moon Base Challenge, inviting U.S. students to develop innovative solutions for building humanity’s first permanent lunar outpost. From power systems to astronaut safety, their ideas could help make long-term life on the Moon possible and pave the way to Mars. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange new world
item.description: A European spacecraft has revealed a mysterious, crater-covered side of the asteroid Didymos as it prepares to investigate the aftermath of NASA’s historic 2022 asteroid impact. The mission could uncover new clues about the collision and help turn asteroid deflection into a powerful defense against future threats to Earth. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Amazon perdió 40 satélites por el lanzamiento fallido del cohete Vulcan
item.description: El hecho marca un revés en la carrera de Jeff Bezos contra Starlink de Elon Musk Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
item.description: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Deep beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists have discovered tiny hidden ecosystems inside metal-rich rocks that take millions of years to form. Researchers examined 244 nodules and found more than 4,100 animals living in their cracks and cavities, including unique communities unlike those in the surrounding seafloor mud. These remarkable miniature habitats could now be threatened by deep-sea mining for valuable metals. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A 19-year study reveals a troubling link between napping and death
item.description: A surprising new study suggests that when and how often older adults nap could reveal hidden warning signs about their health. Researchers followed 1,338 people for up to 19 years and discovered that longer, more frequent naps were linked to higher mortality, while morning nappers faced a 30% greater risk of death than afternoon nappers. Each additional hour of daytime sleep was associated with a 13% increase in mortality risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Por qué mucha de la fibra que necesita tu cuerpo termina en el bote de basura (y cómo aprovecharla mejor en tus comidas)
item.description: Según investigadores de la alimentación, masticar las cáscaras, las semillas y los tallos de las verduras podría proporcionarnos una gran cantidad de fibra que es vital para nuestro organismo. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
item.description: A revolutionary new wearable patch could help people get more restorative sleep without medication or surgery. Developed by University of Texas researchers, the device uses gentle ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions, helping participants enter REM sleep 43 minutes faster and remain there 16 minutes longer on average. The technology also showed promising effects on stress regulation and brain circuits involved in emotion. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI cheating fears spook South Korea ahead of high-stakes college entrance exam
item.description: South Korean officials are scrambling to prevent cheating on a national college entrance exam as concerns grow that artificial intelligence and smart devices are making fraud harder to detect. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX cumple (casi) todo lo prometido con Starship: captura la nave, despliega 26 satélites y falla solo con el propulsor
item.description: Ya lo avisábamos y se ha cumplido, pero solo en parte. SpaceX ha hecho historia con el vuelo 15 de Starship al completar cada uno de sus objetivos de forma casi impecable. El único inconveniente ha sido que no ha logrado recuperar la primera etapa mediante Mechazilla, sino que explotó durante un amerizaje de última hora. La segunda etapa sí la ha capturado mediante sus famosos “palillos chinos”. Puesto que hasta ahora nadie había logrado recuperar de forma controlada la segunda etapa de un cohete mediante este método, podemos decir que, efectivamente, han hecho historia. Los objetivos . Con… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Opening Of Ann Francis Padlock: X-ray scans reveal ANCE code; meaning still unknown
item.description: After four centuries, the 16th-century brass lock from the Ann Francis shipwreck has finally been unlocked. Utilizing cutting-edge micro-CT scanning technology, researchers deciphered the combination as ANCE. This remarkable find is part of a treasure trove uncovered on Margam Beach in South Wales. Though the letters' meaning remains a mystery, the padlock is now proudly exhibited at the National Waterfront Museum, highlighting its importance in maritime history. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Nasa’s Voyager 1 to make history by reaching a light-day from Earth
item.description: On Wednesday, November 18, almost half a century after it lifted off from Cape Canaveral, the Voyager 1 spacecraft will cross a technological and astronomical milestone when it hurtles beyond one light-day’s travel time from Earth. It’s also a 26-billion-kilometre milestone, as that is the approximate distance light covers in 24 hours and how far Voyager 1 has now travelled in what Nasa has described as an “epic” journey since launching on September 5, 1977. The approximately 800kg probe with... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: dpa

item.title: Sabíamos que la misión DART cambió la trayectoria de Dimorphos. Lo que no sabíamos es que también cambió su forma
item.description: A finales de septiembre de 2022, la misión DART ( Double Asteroid Redirection Test ) hacía historia , curiosamente, estampándose contra un asteroide. El hito no estuvo en el impacto en sí sino en lograr con él desviar levemente la trayectoria de un asteroide, Dimorphos. Lo esperado y lo inesperado. En los cuatro años transcurridos desde entonces, hemos ido aprendiendo nuevos detalles sobre los efectos del impacto de DART en el asteroide Dimorphos. Ahora sabemos, por ejemplo, que DART no solo logró desviar la trayectoria orbital de la roca espacial; también consiguió con su impacto hacer que… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Martínez-Juarez

item.title: The Last Ice on Puncak Jaya
item.description: Ice near the summit of the Indonesian mountain peak has shrunk to scattered patches too small to flow like glaciers. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: The secret to building Moon bases may be hiding in emergency blankets
item.description: Scientists have turned the thin plastic used in emergency blankets into remarkably strong insulation that could help astronauts survive the Moon's extreme temperatures. Built from hundreds of stacked layers, the material withstands crushing pressure without losing its thermal protection, potentially paving the way for tougher, longer-lasting lunar habitats. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom
item.description: Scientists have unexpectedly discovered how to control the magnetic spin inside a single atom's nucleus using radio waves, overturning previous assumptions about atomic behavior. The breakthrough could pave the way for more reliable quantum memory, although researchers are still trying to understand why it works. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
item.description: MIT scientists discovered that carefully timed bursts of gentle pink noise during sleep can strengthen the brain’s natural cleaning waves, which help flush away potentially harmful waste. The breakthrough could pave the way for new treatments aimed at improving sleep and memory while potentially reducing the buildup of proteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rocket launch in US fails, destroying payload of 40 Amazon satellites
item.description: A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortly after lift-off from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites from Amazon’s Leo internet network in the launch company’s first mission failure. The rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after lift-off from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, and the cause was not immediately clear. It represented a major setback for the two-decade-old company’s new flagship... Publicado también por: The Verge. Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Why aging stars suffer a sudden luminosity dip
item.description: From a naked-eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. Not much goes on but shining. The sun itself is fairly plain and nondescript and will shine relatively steadily for billions of years. It's considered a low-mass star compared to the most massive stars, which are rarer and contain many times its mass. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites as ULA's Vulcan rocket fails minutes after launch
item.description: Amazon's planned launch of 40 satellites for its Leo internet network failed after the Vulcan rocket malfunctioned. The Vulcan rocket, operated by United Launch Alliance, experienced an anomaly 10 minutes after liftoff. This failure poses a setback for Amazon's satellite internet plans, which aim to compete with Elon Musk's Starlink. Amazon has also invested in other launch options including Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket and Arianespace. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites
item.description: Boeing and Lockheed Martin's rocket venture suffered its first mission failure when a Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites failed to reach orbit. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.
item.dc:creator: BY REUTERS

item.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
item.description: A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago may have helped shape one of the most important differences between humans and our closest relatives: how our brains develop. Scientists at Lund University discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene called LINC00662, which remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in early brain development. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Milk and wine used in Menorcan funerary rituals over 2,000 years ago
item.description: In the Late Iron Age, or post-Talayotic period, over 2,000 years ago, Menorca and the other Balearic Islands experienced increasing connectivity with the wider Mediterranean. However, they also maintained distinctive local funerary traditions, such as burying their loved ones in rock-cut tombs, or artificial caves. Some of these caves contained external courtyards located in front of the burial chambers where animal offerings might have been made. Archaeologists even suspect that perishable foods or liquids were offered in characteristic island containers, such as high-bottomed vessels. Until… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: School environment plays key role in shaping parents' educational hopes for their children, suggests study
item.description: Where segregation is high, the school a child attends is closely linked to how many years of education parents expect their child to go on to complete. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Archaeologists uncover a witness to the Neolithic revolution
item.description: Radiocarbon dating and isotope analysis of an immaculately preserved skeleton from Mesolithic Denmark indicate that the individual lived through the introduction of agriculture and adapted his diet to the change, providing a unique "eyewitness account" of one of humanity's most significant technological revolutions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Nature, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03715-7 Researchers must track warming oceans and use the knowledge gained to inform strategies for sustaining fisheries and communities that depend on them. Fuente: Nature.

item.description: Nature, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03712-w A lack of crosstalk between research disciplines is hampering scholars’ ability to fully examine how people have altered Earth’s biodiversity. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
item.description: This was the first total mission failure in United Launch Alliance's 20-year history. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: When the Saudi desert was green: A 125,000-year-old lakeside reveals how early humans lived
item.description: Megafauna remains, stone tools and rare plant material recovered from the 125,000-year-old lakeside site of Uruq al-Julaybah in Mundafan, southern Saudi Arabia, provide one of the most detailed pictures yet of prehistoric human life in Arabia. Together, the discoveries reveal how early people lived, hunted and used their environment during a greener, wetter period in Arabian history. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
item.description: United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon's competitor to SpaceX's Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink […] Fuente: The Verge.

item.description: Article URL: https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/ula-vulcan-centaur-return-to-flight-amazon-leo-internet-satellite-launch Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50510442 Points: 117 # Comments: 62 Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.

item.title: Dark matter–hunting satellite Euclid reveals record number of cosmic 'magnifying glasses'
item.description: UBC researchers have helped uncover 15,000 new potential strong gravitational lenses—the largest collection of these cosmic tools that help astronomers investigate dark matter. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 12-year study finds declining elephant numbers lead to fragmented social networks
item.description: A study in Udawalawe National Park indicates that dwindling elephant groups result in significant social vulnerabilities. With fewer individuals, elephants transition from larger communities to smaller, more isolated factions, which impairs their capacity to nurture and feed effectively. Once a critical social threshold is exceeded, the difficulty of reversing such fragmentation intensifies. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: The experiments improving our understanding of volcanic tsunamis
item.description: Tsunamis triggered by volcanic eruptions are poorly understood because of the complex dynamics governing how falling rocks and ash interact with seawater to generate waves. As a result, it is difficult to anticipate whether a volcanic flow will trigger a tsunami and, if so, how big it will be. Researchers have used laboratory experiments to study this process, but little is known about how well these models mimic reality. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Minting Accident: 3D tests suggest sixpence was deformed during minting; cause remains inconclusive
item.description: A team of researchers has thoroughly examined a distorted silver sixpence from 1834, uncovering unexpected manufacturing flaws. Through intricate 3D imaging, they revealed significant deformations and patterns that stray from regular wear. This peculiar state of the coin prompts a deeper look into the production methods of the steam-powered minting period. The analysis, combining advanced imaging and chemistry, sheds light on historical minting defects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tangled quantum whirlpools caught unraveling in an ultracold gas
item.description: When a cloud of atoms is cooled close to absolute zero, its atoms can merge into a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC): an exotic fluid in which atoms across the whole cloud share a single quantum state. Current theories predict that as a disordered quantum gas settles into this ordered state, a tangle of tiny vortices should form and gradually unravel. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Giant, prehistoric rodent fossils discovered in southern Thailand
item.description: An international team of paleontologists, including researchers from McGill University, has discovered "remarkably large" rodent fossils in the pit of a mine in southern Thailand. The finding, published in Scientific Reports, provides a new perspective on the early manifestation of rodent gigantism—the process by which animals evolve to become larger—demonstrating that the evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents is considerably older and more geographically widespread than previously recognized, the researchers said. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
item.description: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe
item.description: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-mass, metal-poor, star-forming galaxy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event
item.description: NASA scientists warn that the rapidly intensifying 2026 El Niño could surpass the historic 1997-98 event, which triggered devastating weather extremes around the world. Satellite data reveal striking similarities between the two, raising the possibility of major rainfall and flooding this winter, although the exact impacts remain uncertain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Uranus and Neptune’s bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained
item.description: The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s. New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields. Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
item.description: Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan, harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nations grapple with loss of 1.5C target at UN climate summit
item.description: The world has already warmed about 1.4°C above pre-industrial times and the UN declared in September that crossing 1.5°C — the most ambitious target threshold of the Paris accord — was imminent and unavoidable Publicado también por: The Hindu - International. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
item.description: SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. Publicado también por: The Independent - World. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Astronomers discover a dead star spinning every 8 minutes and sending mysterious radio pulses
item.description: Scientists have discovered a strange stellar pair more than 5,000 light-years away, where a dead star spinning every eight minutes produces mysterious radio pulses while orbiting a Sun-like star. The breakthrough also revealed massive magnetic storms on the companion star, offering fresh clues to one of astronomy's emerging mysteries. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ALMA reveals three star-forming cores at different stages inside one gas clump
item.description: Astronomers have revealed three dense cores at different evolutionary stages within the massive star-forming region G40.282−0.219, shedding light on the physical and chemical differences among cores within the same massive dense clump. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections. Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors and improved viral infection outcomes in mice. Even more remarkably, giving mice arginine after they contracted influenza helped them recover. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists have drawn a treasure map of where fossils of ancient sea life are still to be found
item.description: In an exciting development, researchers have pinpointed potential hotspots for fossil discoveries that remain undocumented. Focusing on the Cenozoic Era, celebrated for its rich marine biodiversity, this study seeks to enhance fossil hunting by concentrating efforts on less explored territories. Additionally, revisiting collections from natural history museums could yield new insights into ancient species, reinforcing the pursuit of understanding marine life from the past. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: More Nobel winners, less innovation? Chinese study reveals cost of top-tier awards
item.description: Science prizes usually put the spotlight on winners, celebrating their discoveries but paying little attention to the researchers left out. A study by scientists at the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has found that prominent innovation awards may discourage colleagues from pursuing unconventional research – with the most prestigious prizes having the strongest negative effect. The findings raise questions about the wider consequences of scientific honours, including the Nobel Prize, as... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Chao Kong

item.title: Evolutionary threat: Chinese mountain birds lost nearly half genetic diversity in 50 years
item.description: Genetic diversity is nature’s insurance policy – an evolutionary safety net that provides the building blocks for natural selection. While members of the same species share a mostly identical genome, a sliver of unique genetic variants determines their individual traits. When this diversity erodes, and a population becomes more uniform, it could leave them vulnerable to the same threats and unable to adapt when new ones emerge. In China, scientists have found that common songbird species were... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela

item.title: Christina Koch, de Artemis II, sobre la repercusión de la misión: “Superó con creces todo lo que habíamos imaginado y esperado”
item.description: Tras su regreso a la Tierra, Donald Trump le entregó a cada tripulante una medalla Medalla de Honor Espacial del Congreso, durante una ceremonia en el Centro Espacial Jonhson de Houston Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
item.description: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins
item.description: A groundbreaking drone survey has revealed a startling split in the fate of New Zealand's endangered Erect-crested penguins. While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions. Even more surprisingly, the tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands, despite being 40 times smaller. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion
item.description: The coalition, launched in the Colombian coastal city of Santa Marta in April, is expected to release a progress report this week outlining steps taken by participating countries, including additional national plans to reduce dependence on coal, oil and gas Publicado también por: The Independent - World. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
item.description: Dinosaurs may have been snacking on seaweed and other ocean foods more than 100 million years ago, according to surprising new evidence hidden in their fossilized teeth. Researchers discovered chemical signatures suggesting that coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals relied partly on nutrients originating in the sea. The findings reveal that marine resources traveled through ancient food chains, supplementing the diets of everything from plant-eating dinosaurs to predators. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers
item.description: Scientists have discovered how to use flashes of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions inside a crystal, solving a decades-old mystery about how the material behaves. The laser-induced alignment lasts just a trillionth of a second, but the breakthrough could open the door to new ways of processing and storing information. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breaking objects that shone with the brightness of a trillion Suns when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Powered by supermassive black holes, these extraordinary cosmic beacons reveal a time when the first galaxies were still taking shape. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Is this iconic black hole image accurate? New study delivers an independent result
item.description: On April 10, 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) Collaboration revealed the first picture of a black hole. The object is at the center of a galaxy known as M87, about 55 million light-years away. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there's a catch
item.description: It felt like stepping into the future. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship rocket in huge milestone for the space industry
item.description: The historic first gets SpaceX closer to “rapid reusability” of rockets. Fuente: MarketWatch.
item.dc:creator: Emily Bary

item.title: Hundreds of men march in Switzerland to protest violence against women
item.description: Organisers say men must speak out, as Swiss study finds half of men aged 18 to 24 hold restrictive view of masculinity. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: SpaceX logra por primera vez atrapar la parte superior del cohete Starship en su regreso a la Tierra
item.description: La nave fue capturada en el aire mediante unos enormes brazos mecánicos apodados "palillos chinos". Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Rumbo a la Luna y Marte: afirman que la nave Starship completó 14 vueltas a la Tierra y fue atrapada en su regreso
item.description: La histórica recuperación de la aeronave de acero inoxidable apunta a la reutilización del vehículo para un reciclaje rápido y de bajo costo. El hito fue celebrado por la NASA, la agencia espacial del gobierno de Estados Unidos que financia el proyecto para llevar astronautas a la superficie lunar a través de las misiones Artemis. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.
item.dc:creator: Clarin.com - Home

item.title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
item.description: Starship Test Flight 15 marked the first time Elon Musk's company tried to catch both the booster and upper stage of the rocket. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: SpaceX recupera por primera vez en la historia la nave principal de un cohete espacial
item.description: La empresa de Elon Musk recuperó la segunda etapa de su megacohete Starship, una maniobra inédita en la ingeniería aeroespacial Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: SpaceX rocket orbits Earth and returns to launch pad in world first
item.description: The successful return of the SpaceX rocket to its launch pad is a breakthrough in the company's decade-long effort to develop a fully reusable rocket. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: 2 Infants buried in Peru about 1,600 years ago; one had a rare fatal birth defect called cyclopia
item.description: In southern Peru, archaeologists uncovered the remains of two infants buried together, one exhibiting cyclopia. Genetic analysis confirmed that the infant with cyclopia had trisomy 13, a chromosomal condition. Their burial in a single ceramic vessel reveals insights into ancient funerary practices. Researchers highlighted that the infant's condition did not result in unusual treatment in life or death. This discovery emphasizes the historical presence of congenital differences in human populations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
item.description: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks". Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Urban expansion causes ecological collapse in streams in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area
item.description: The advance of urbanization in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area in Brazil is causing the collapse of food webs in local streams. A study published in August in the journal Nature Cities reveals that the impact of the metropolis goes far beyond a simple reduction in species. Degradation selectively eliminates organisms based on their size and simplifies ecological interactions. Networks of 190 connections plummet to just three. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers track Carnaby's cockatoos in Western Australia; find native habitat helps in conservation
item.description: Urbanization is significantly impacting the habitats of Carnaby's cockatoos in Western Australia. Research indicates that these birds are forced to travel longer distances in search of food across divided landscapes. Even minor patches of native vegetation play a vital role as connections between larger habitats. It's essential for conservation initiatives to prioritize these smaller areas to safeguard wildlife. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: The Brisbane buildings made from sandstone touched by dinosaurs
item.description: Fossilised footprints belonging to 230-million-year-old dinosaurs have been unearthed in Brisbane, indented into the same sandstone that constructed the city's most recognisable buildings. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Loram

item.title: A dead star is flashing radio waves every 8 minutes, and its partner looks a lot like the sun
item.description: Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzling over a new kind of cosmic object called long-period radio transients. These are objects that emit bright flashes of radio waves into space every few minutes to every few hours. Some have been traced back to binary systems consisting of a small, dim, cool star called a red dwarf in orbit with a stellar remnant called a white dwarf. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La inédita captura de Starship: el intento de regresar la nave de SpaceX a la Tierra
item.description: La nave espacial Starship de SpaceX regresó este sábado 14 de noviembre de su vuelo orbital más largo hasta la fecha a la torre de Texas desde la que fue lanzada en la víspera. Se trata de un evento inédito que muestra la primera recuperación clave de la pieza central del sistema de cohetes, en el mayor esfuerzo de una década para desarrollar un cohete totalmente reutilizable. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: Does your culture shape how you look at art? What an eye‑tracking study in Sudan revealed
item.description: Today, Old Dongola is an abandoned settlement on the banks of the Nile in northern Sudan. Hundreds of years ago, however, this place looked very different. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for a new distance record
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space. Publicado también por: Al Jazeera English. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A cosmic magnifying glass could reveal the same supernova two more times in roughly 70 years
item.description: Thanks to the gravitational lensing caused by a massive galaxy cluster and high-resolution images from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers discovered an exploding star when the universe was 4.9 billion years old. The discovery paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 23, presents a prediction for when the rest of the distorted images of SN Ares will arrive. Fuente: Phys.org.
